summary: Petition under Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Section 79(1)(c) & (d) _(d) Condone any inadvertent errors omissions/errors/shortcomings and permit the Petitioner to add/change/modify/alter these filings and make further submissions as may be required at a future date; and/or_ _(e) Pass any such other order/orders, as may be deemed fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.”_ 2. On receipt of the present Petition, the Bid Process Coordinator (hereinafter referred to as “the BPC”), REC Power Development and Consultancy Limited (hereinafter referred to as “RECPDCL”), vide letter dated 5.5.2025, was directed to submit the relevant documents regarding the complete process of the competitive bidding. The necessary details have been filed by the BPC under an affidavit dated 13.5.2025. 3. On 20.5.2025, notice was issued to the Respondents to file their respective replies. During the course of the hearing, the Bid Process Coordinator (BPC), i.e., RECPDCL, was directed to furnish the break-up of the initial acquisition price and the final acquisition price, along with reasons for escalation therein. (c) Upon conclusion of the bid process, the final acquisition price is communicated to the successful bidder after incorporating the actual expenditures incurred under the SPV. The same amount is defined in the Share Purchase Agreement, which is executed between the BPC and the selected bidder. 5. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the BPC has filed the compliance affidavit as directed vide RoP dated 20.5.2025. Accordingly, the matter was reserved for orders. However, no reply has been received from the Respondents despite notice. 6. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner, BPC, and CTUIL and perused the documents available on record. Section 63 of the Act provides as under: (c) The BPC shall prepare the bid documents in accordance with the Guidelines and obtain approval of the Appropriate Government, or alternatively, (f) Standard documentation to be provided in the RfP shall include definitions of requirements including brief description of the Project, commissioning milestones to be achieved by the bidders, qualification requirements to be met by the bidders including, minimum net worth, etc. with necessary proof of the same, as outlined in the bid documents, Specified target dates/months for commissioning and commercial operations, Standard Transmission Service Agreement (TSA), agreement(s) under the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Sharing of Inter State Transmission Charges and Losses) Regulations as amended from time to time, period of validity of offer of bidder, TSA proposed to be entered with the SPV including Order in Petition No. 434/AT/2025 bid opening committee in the presence of the bid evaluation committee. The bidder who has quoted the lowest transmission charge as per the evaluation procedure shall be considered for the award. (k) BPC shall make the final result of evaluation of all bids public. The final TSA, along with the certification by the bid evaluation committee, shall be forwarded to the Appropriate Commission, for the adoption of tariff discovered from the quoted annual transmission charges during the e-reverse bidding process in terms of Section 63 of the Act. 8. Therefore, we have to examine whether the Guidelines issued by the Central Government have been followed in the present case in a transparent process of bidding. 12. BPC started the process of selection of the successful bidder with the publication of a Global Invitation for Qualification for the selection of a developer on a BOOT basis for the Project. The notice of the RfP was published in National/International newspapers on 26.9.2024, with the last date of submission of response to RfP as 3.1.2025. Intimation regarding the initiation of the bid process was given to this Commission on 26.9.2024 in accordance with Clause 4.2 of the Guidelines dated 10.8.2021. |**S. No. **|**Events**|**Date**| |---|---|---| |1.|Publication of RfP|26.9.2024| |2.|Intimation to the Commission|26.9.2024| |3.|RFP (Technical)& Price Bid Submission|3.1.2025| |4.|RFP (Technical) Bid Opening|3.1.2025| |5.|RFP (Financial) Initial Price Offer-Opening|22.1.2025| |6.|e-Reverse Auction|23.1.2025| |7.|No. of Bidders participated in the e-Reverse Auction| 4 bidders participated (mentioned in para 18)| |8.|Rounds of E-Reverse Auction|31 rounds| |9.|Final Bid Evaluation Committee Meeting|20.2.2025| |10.|Issuance of the LoI|28.2.2025| |11.|Signingof Agreements & transfer of SPV|24.3.2025| |12.|Estimated Cost of the Project|Rs. 1,407.44 Million| 20. The Letter of Intent was issued by the BPC on 28.2.2025 to the successful bidder, i.e., IndiGrid 2 Private Limited. In accordance with Clause 12.3 of the Guidelines, the BPC has hosted on the website of RECPDCL the final result of the evaluation of the bids for the selection of a developer for the Project. 21. In accordance with the provisions of the bid documents and upon the issuance of LoI to the successful bidder (IndiGrid 2 Private Limited) and acquisition of the SPV (the Petitioner) by the successful bidder, the Petitioner has prayed for the adoption of transmission charges for the Project, which has been discovered through the competitive bidding process. 22. In accordance with Clause 2.15.2 of the RfP, the selected bidder shall, within 10 days of the issue of the Letter of Intent, accomplish the following tasks: clause (a) of sub-section (5) of Section 15 of the Act, inviting suggestions/ objections to the proposal of the Commission. _7. Based on deliberations and considering the factors indicated at Para (6) above, BEC recommends for issuance of the Letter of Intent (LOI) to the successful bidder i.e. M/s IndiGrid 2 Private Limited based on the tariff discovered through e-Reverse Auction concluded on 23.01.2025._
